string.text: {=aom_anduinvale_desc}The Beornings keep the upper vale of the Anduin between the Misty Mountains and Mirkwood, a folk of farmers, herdsmen and honey-keepers who share the river meadows with the Woodmen of the Vales. They hold the Carrock and the Old Ford, take no toll from honest travellers and a heavy one from orcs and wolves. Their chieftains are chosen for strength and plain speech, and they follow no king into a war that is not their own.

{=aom_angaladh_desc}The Woodmen of Angáladh live under the western eaves of Mirkwood, where their fathers cleared steads among trees so hard that axes ring on them like iron. They are bowmen, woodcutters and hunters, few in number and slow to trust, at peace with the Elves of the northern wood. Every year the shadow in the south of the forest grows, and every year their king sends more of his archers to watch the Narrows.

{=aom_arthedain_desc}The Dúnedain of Arthedain are the last heirs of Arnor, the North-kingdom Elendil founded. From Fornost upon the North Downs the line of Arvedui still keeps the watch that Isildur's heirs have kept for a thousand years, though their towns are few, their lords are poor and the shadow of Angmar never leaves the hills. They are fewer than their southern kin and prouder than their numbers warrant, and every season the wild lands press closer.

{=aom_bluecraig_desc}The goblins of Blue Craig hold the western spurs of the Ered Luin, cut off from their kin under the Ered Luin by the length of Eriador. They raid the Dwarf-roads and the shores of Lune, and the Elves of Mithlond count them the nearer enemy.

{=aom_cardolan_desc}The Dúnedain of Cardolan hold the south of old Arnor, the plains and river country between the Baranduin and the Greyflood. Their kings lie in the barrows of Tyrn Gorthad, their barges still come up to Tharbad, and their riders are the best of the three northern kingdoms. Their towns are few and their lords quarrel with Arthedain and Rhudaur over the old crown, while the wild lands grow bolder every year.

{=aom_dolguldur_desc}Dol Guldur is a fortress of shadow and malice. Once a stronghold of Sauron in Mirkwood, it is now ruled by the Necromancer's dark lieutenants. The armies of Dol Guldur are a fearsome blend of orcs, wargs, and dark sorcery. This bastion of evil corrupts the forest around it, spreading decay and despair. The warriors of Dol Guldur are relentless, driven by the will of their dark master.

{=aom_dorwinion_desc}The Men of Dorwinion tend the vineyards on the warm slopes above the Sea of Rhûn, and their wine goes up the Redwater and the River Running to the halls of Elves and Men far to the west. They are vintners, boatmen and river traders, a Northman folk who would rather sell to a stranger than fight him. Their king keeps his court at Vineholm, and every year the Easterlings across the inland sea look harder at his rich and lightly guarded land.

{=aom_erebor_desc}The Longbeards of Erebor are a proud and industrious race, dwelling in the halls of the Lonely Mountain. Masters of craftsmanship and mining, they are renowned for their skill in forging weapons, armor, and treasures of unrivaled beauty. Led by their King under the Mountain, the dwarves of Erebor are a resilient people, fiercely protective of their homeland and its riches.

{=aom_eredluin_desc}The dwarves of Ered Luin dwell in the Blue Mountains at the western edge of Middle-earth. Durin's Folk came there in exile and made Thorin's Halls, and in this age the Broadbeams and the Firebeards keep Belegost and Nogrod again, the oldest dwarf-cities of the West. They are miners and smiths, poorer than their kin in the east, and they trade iron with the Elves of Lindon and the Men of Eriador while the goblins of Blue Craig gnaw at their roads.

{=aom_goblin_desc}The Goblins of Goblin-town swarm the tunnels beneath the High Pass of the Misty Mountains. Cowardly alone but overwhelming in number, they breed endlessly in the dark and pour out to ambush travellers on the mountain roads. Under their Great Goblin and his captains they harry Elves, Dwarves, and Men alike, serving the growing Shadow for plunder and spite.

{=aom_gondor_desc}The people of Gondor are a proud and resilient folk, heirs to the greatest kingdom of Men in Middle-earth. Founded by the Númenórean exiles Isildur and Anárion, Gondor stands as a bastion of strength and hope against the encroaching darkness of Mordor. Its stone cities, crowned by the majestic Minas Tirith, are marvels of engineering and endurance. Guided by noble stewards and valiant captains, they field disciplined armies of steadfast infantry and swift mounted knights, a shining beacon of defiance in the face of despair.

{=aom_gundabad_desc}The Gundabad Orcs of the Misty Mountains are savage and relentless. From the ancient stronghold of Mount Gundabad, they raid the surrounding lands, driven by a thirst for vengeance and conquest. Under the rule of powerful chieftains, they amass legions of goblins, wargs, and trolls. Gundabad's warriors are brutish and cunning, masters of ambush and overwhelming force.

{=aom_isengard_desc}The people of Isengard are Saruman's legions, forged through industry and fueled by a dark vision of domination. Centered around the impenetrable tower of Orthanc, Isengard is home to the Uruk-hai, bred for strength, endurance, and obedience. With machines of war and the cunning of their master, they crush all opposition with ruthless precision.

{=aom_lindon_desc}The Falathrim of Lindon are the last of the Sindar shipwrights, dwelling at Mithlond where the Gulf of Lune meets the sea. Círdan has kept the Grey Havens since the First Age, and it is from his quays that the white ships pass into the West.

{=aom_lothlorien_desc}The Elves of Lothlórien, known as the Galadhrim, are a noble and enigmatic people dwelling in the Golden Wood. Guided by the wisdom and power of Lady Galadriel and Lord Celeborn, they are guardians of one of the last bastions of elven beauty and tranquility in Middle-earth. The Galadhrim are unmatched archers, blending seamlessly with the golden Mallorn trees of their homeland.

{=aom_mirkwood_desc}The Silvan Elves of Mirkwood, also known as the Woodland Realm, are a proud and resilient people who call the vast forest their home. Ruled by King Thranduil, they are skilled hunters and warriors, navigating the shadowed woods with unmatched agility and precision. The Mirkwood Elves are masters of the bow, striking swiftly and silently from the trees.

{=aom_mistymountainorcs_desc}The Orcs of the Misty Mountains are a savage war-host dwelling among the high peaks and deep places of the range. Driven by an ancient hatred of Elves and Dwarves, they muster vast and ill-armed legions and fall upon the lands below, serving the dark powers that stir in the East.

{=aom_mordor_desc}The Orcs of Mordor are a brutal and relentless force, bred in the dark pits of Barad-dûr to serve the will of Sauron. Cruel and savage, they march to war in endless hordes, wielding crude but deadly weapons forged in the fires of Mount Doom. Clad in jagged armor and bearing black banners emblazoned with the Red Eye, they bring fear and destruction wherever they tread. Bound by the iron will of their Dark Lord, the Orcs of Mordor are divided into warbands led by ruthless captains, united only in their desire for conquest.

{=aom_rhudaur_desc}Rhudaur is the hill kingdom of old Arnor, between the Hoarwell and the Loudwater. Its Dúnedain lords hold the Angle and the tower of Cameth Brin and rule a people of hill-men who never loved the West. The line of its first king still endures, but its holds are cold, its fells are full of trolls, and the orcs of the mountains watch every pass.

{=aom_rivendell_desc}The Noldor Elves of Rivendell are a wise and ancient people, renowned for their unmatched knowledge, artistry, and valor. Under the guidance of Lord Elrond, they preserve the fading beauty and lore of the Elder Days within the hidden sanctuary of Imladris. Masters of both the sword and the bow, the Noldor combine martial skill with the grace and precision of their kind.

{=aom_southrhovanion_desc}The Northmen of South Rhovanion ride the wide plains between the southern eaves of Mirkwood and the Brown Lands, a free people of horse-breeders who count the Éothéod of the north as their kin. Their fathers were the lords of the Northmen in the days of the old kings, and the barrows of those kings still stand on the grasslands. Twice the Wainriders came out of the East with wagon and fire and broke them, and the riders of the plains have not forgotten it.

{=aom_umbar_desc}The people of Umbar are seafaring warriors and corsairs, masters of the seas south of Gondor. Descended from Númenórean exiles, they are known for their cunning and ferocity in battle. Under black sails, their fleets raid the coasts, striking fear into the hearts of their enemies. While their allegiances lie with Sauron, the Corsairs of Umbar are fiercely independent, valuing strength and cunning above all.
